newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end mixed, banks hit ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end mixed, banks hit ahead of jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks stuttered to a mixed finish with interest-rate sensitive issues slammed by a bond market sell-off amid heightened anxiety ahead of Friday's key November employment report.

"Bonds are selling off in anticipation of a strong jobs report after a tremendous amount of good news was absorbed. Equities are gyrating after a tremendous run-up," said Lehman Brothers Global Economic Advisors chief economist Allen Sinai.
The Dow industrials rose 15 to about 6438 after two days of losses. The long bond slumped 1-13/32 to yield 6.50 percent.

The long bond yield's jump from 6.40 percent at Wednesday's close fuelled further profit-taking in financials and other interest-rate sensitive stocks. Major banks were especially hard-hit after their spectacular run-up this year. Citicorp shed 4-1/4 to 101-5/8, BankAmerica lost three to 96-1/2 and Wells Fargo was off 2-3/4 to 272-1/2.
In the broader market, the S&P 500 fell one to about 744 and the Nasdaq Composite rose three to 1300.
Losers barely beat winners on very heavy NYSE volume of about 482 million shares.
A November non-farm payrolls reading of 179,000 is seen.

"People are afraid of Friday's number and the revision to third-quarter non-farm productivity to down 0.3 percent from up 0.2 percent was not exactly good. Jobless claims fell 8,000" and signalled an unexpectedly strong labor market, said Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst.

Sinai said Lehman was expecting a non-farm payrolls to come in at 170,000 to 200,000. "We think the report will be solid and expect the economy to pick up some. That might be a caution flag for the bond market."
As for the stock market, Sinai said, "We might have topped out near term and will consolidate in the 6300-6500 range."
He added, "It's still a bull market. The economy still looks terrific. Interest rates, even if they go up some, it won't be by a lot and the markets will adjust to that."

Ken Ducey, head of trading at BT Brokerage, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bankers Trust, said, "The market has acted very well since we're off 100 points (since Tuesday) and rallied back Wednesday. The market is trying to find a spot here. I think it will move higher."
Retailers were mostly weaker after reporting, as expected, strong November sales ahead of the all-important holiday shopping season.

Sears slipped 1/4 to 49 after reporting November same-store sales fell 0.7 percent and Wal-mart fell 1/8 to 25-1/2 after same-store sales rose four percent last month. But Dayton-Hudson rose 5/8 to 39-7/8 after November same-store sales rose 1.3 percent.
Gymboree slumped 4-5/8 to 23-1/8 after reporting November same-store sales fell 15 percent. Morgan Stanley and Alex Brown downgraded the children's apparel retailer.
Sunglass maker Oakley Inc shed 3-7/8 to 11-1/2 after forecasting below-consensus quarterly earnings amid further delays in orders from its key customer Sunglass Hut.
Sunglass Hut fell 7/8 to 7-3/8 after reporting November same-store sales fell 3.4 percent.
Among other shares, Input/Output rose 2-5/8 to 18-3/4, rebounding somewhat from a 7-1/2 point drop Wednesday on an earnings warning.

Santa Fe Pacific Gold surged three to 14-7/8 and Newmont Mining lost 3/8 to 47-1/8. Newmont offered to acquire Santa Fe for $2 billion in a tax-free stock swap that would create the largest gold company in North America.
Compaq Computer rose 2-1/2 to 84-1/4. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell raised earnings estimates for the company.
Great Lakes Chemical lost three to 49-1/8. The company Wednesday forecast a flat 1997 performance. Prudential and CS First Boston downgraded the stock.
ThreeCom surged three to 79-3/4. Hambrecht & Quist started coverage of the stock with a strong buy rating.
Anchor Gaming climbed five to 46 after retaining Morgan Stanley as financial adviser to review alternatives to boost shareholder value, including the possible sale or merger of the company.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 3.10 to 1300.12.
The S&P 500 fell 0.72 to 744.38.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street Desk 212-859-1721
